stories.headline: Duck the Eighth Arrives in Person; Mrs. Holt Declines to Say Which One Is for Lucy; Lucy Already Knows
stories.byline: By our Ridge and Hollow correspondent
body: Elspeth Holt, 81, keeper of the eastern ridge and presiding authority on the proper haberdashery of enchanted rubber ducks, appeared at the household's front step at half past nine this morning carrying a canvas bag, a second canvas bag, and the air of someone who had decided to come and so had come.

Duck the eighth was unwrapped from oilcloth on the doorstep and presented without ceremony: a soft woollen tam-o'-shanter in heathered green, with a small sprig of dried rowan pinned to the brim. The accompanying note read, in full: 'Not the detective. The other one.' The household has confirmed it does not know what this means. Lucy has confirmed nothing, but relocated to a different room at a pace witnesses have described as 'deliberate.'

Mrs. Holt took tea, admired the kitchen shelf without being told about the bracket debate, and departed before lunch. Four ducks remain at the ridge. Steve has updated the hat log to include a new column: 'Intended Recipient (Disputed).'

serial.title: The Six Remaining Ducks of Elspeth Holt

stories.headline: Tuesday's Ledger Runs Long; Christine Runs Longer; Ledger Blinks First
stories.byline: By our Diagon Alley financial correspondent
body: A Tuesday queue that arrived with what one goblin supervisor privately called 'a worrying level of ambient grievance' was nonetheless processed, resolved, and sent home in good order by mid-afternoon, following what sources describe as a sustained display of patience so precise it constituted a tactical manoeuvre.

One account-holder arrived with a folder. Christine arrived with a better folder. The matter was settled on page two of Christine's folder; the account-holder's folder was not opened. He has been invited to return Thursday if he still has questions. He is not expected to have questions.

stories.headline: Steve Turns Attention to the Side Gate; Gate Opens; Gate Closes; Gate Opens Again in the Correct Direction
body: The side gate, which has opened inward when it was meant to open outward for a period now estimated at between two and four years, has been rehung, re-latched, and tested at speed by Steve, who reports that it now swings true on both the entry and the exit and does not catch on the post.

The enchanted Jeep, parked nearby during the operation, was observed to shift slightly on its wheels at the moment the gate swung correctly for the first time — a movement one household member characterised as 'quiet approval.' The gate has been informed it is on probation.

stories.headline: Tibbs Submits a Second Opinion; Second Opinion Is the Same as the First; Nobody Is Surprised; Tibbs Appears Satisfied
stories.byline: Ministry correspondent, filing from the corridor
body: Cornelius Tibbs, non-voting member of the now technically active but practically dormant Standing Consultative Committee on Broadly Geographic and Adjacent Matters, submitted a two-paragraph memorandum to the Committee's acting secretary this afternoon. The memorandum, titled 'Further Observations,' contained observations consistent in all material respects with his previous memorandum, titled 'Observations.'

The Committee's acting secretary has logged the document and added it to the archive. The archive has not responded. Tibbs has been seen leaving the Ministry building with the expression of a man who considers the day well spent. The puddle on the eastern end of Diagon Alley was culverted as scheduled. It has been confirmed as gone.

familiars_corner: Lucy: Relocated to the reading chair following Mrs. Holt's visit and has not moved since. When asked about the note ('Not the detective. The other one.'), Lucy looked at the wall. The wall also did not answer.

Ellie: Greeted Mrs. Holt as warmly as she greeted her last time, and the time before that, and with exactly as much prior recognition of her as a previously known individual, which is to say: none. Mrs. Holt appeared charmed. Ellie is now asleep in the beam of light near the window, having befriended it successfully.

Jersey: Secured a position on Mrs. Holt's lap before she had fully sat down and remained there for the duration of the visit. Mrs. Holt did not object. Jersey has filed this under 'new regular arrangement' and looks forward to her next visit accordingly.
founding_editor_note: That gate should've been rehung in 2021, but I'll allow it. Good latch placement. — D.

in_brief.sport: The Tuesday morning carry — one canvas bag per arm, up the front path — went unwitnessed by any official scorer, which is a shame.
in_brief.forecast: Warm and unhurried through Wednesday; a duck expected before Thursday; the deerstalker question remains open, pending feline cooperation.

storyline_updates.title: The Six Remaining Ducks of Elspeth Holt
storyline_updates.summary: Day 4: Duck the eighth has arrived — a heathered tam-o'-shanter with a rowan sprig — delivered by Mrs. Holt in person. The note read 'Not the detective. The other one.' Lucy relocated immediately; the household remains uncertain. Steve's hat log now includes a 'Intended Recipient (Disputed)' column. Mrs. Holt had tea, admired the shelf, and left. Four ducks remain. Day 5 (resolution): Mrs. Holt should arrive with the final duck — or the final ducks — and the scene should be the quiet, full-circle moment the arc has been building toward. The 'detective' question (the deerstalker) and 'not the detective, the other one' (the tam) should be resolved — almost certainly landing on Lucy and Jersey respectively, or reversed to comic effect. The completion should feel like a small ceremony: all eleven ducks on the Jeep, all hatted, Mrs. Holt satisfied, nothing more to do but stand there and look at it. Warm, final, and without fuss.
